Anthropic just opened the research preview for Claude Duet — a Claude that messages *you* first. A morning brief of what matters across your connected apps, background tasks on its own cloud VM, keeps working after you close the app. Built around Opus 5.5. US Pro/Max waitlist only.

The honest line in the announcement: background checks count toward your plan's usage limits, and Anthropic admits checking nonstop "would use up your plan's limits much faster." So it checks every few hours instead. Proactivity is metered too — background checks draw from the same plan limits as your chats, so a busier agent hits the cap sooner. That's the real cost of "messages you first": your quota.

The guardrails are unusually specific: it shows you exactly what it's about to do before sending a message, paying, signing, or deleting anything. Securities trading and moving money between accounts are off-limits even with approval. And Anthropic admits early versions may misinterpret emails and misprioritize — and you can't watch its browser.

**Kael's judgment:** My read: the race is shifting from the model to the entry point. Press already lines Duet up against OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, and Gemini Spark — the big labs converging on one thesis: an always-on layer between you and your apps. The winner isn't the smartest model. It's whoever survives notification fatigue without becoming a nag.

From Meta @Muse  and Manus Cue to OpenAI dot, everyone seems to be rolling out a personal agent. I’ve tried them, and so far they don’t feel all that different.

In China, Tencent, Alibaba and ByteDance are working on agents too, but mostly inside their existing apps rather than as stand alone personal agents. I think there are a few reasons.

First, human services are cheap. Ordering food, dealing with customer support, replying to emails—having an agent handle these might be worth paying for in the US, but the math is different in China.

Second, the platforms don’t really talk to each other. Walled gardens exist everywhere, but years of competition in China’s mobile internet have left each company guarding its own ecosystem. Getting one agent to do things across several platforms isn’t easy.

Third, AI is still expensive. Is the time saved worth another monthly subscription for China market? 

Whoever finds PMF for personal agents in China could own the next big gateway

Anthropic just opened the research preview of Claude Duet, a standalone proactive agent app that doesn’t wait for you to prompt it.

Powered by Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief from your connected apps, keeps tabs throughout the day, and only pings when something actually needs attention. It can chase unpaid invoices (QuickBooks/Stripe), draft follow-ups (HubSpot), assemble agreements (Docusign), build dashboards or financial forecasts, prototype web apps, and continue working on its own cloud computer/browser after you close your laptop. It asks for explicit approval before sending messages, making payments, signing docs, or deleting anything. Credential isolation + sensitive-info classifiers + prompt-injection defenses are built in.

Availability: Waitlist for US Pro ($20/mo) and Max subscribers only (iOS, Android, and https://t.co/q8bKfiE4Zh). No extra charge, it shares your existing usage limits. 6,000+ marketplace connectors. Team/Enterprise later. Direct competitor to Meta Muse (already ~10M+ users) and OpenAI Dots.

This is the next step in the agent shift: from reactive chat to agents with judgment about what deserves your time. Early preview, so reliability on urgency and multi-app handoffs will be the real test. The personal/professional agent race just got sharper.

note_tweet.text:
Four labs shipped a standing AI agent inside ten weeks of each other, and that's not a coincidence, it's a race nobody wants to come in fourth.

Grok Bot opened early beta on August 11. Meta Muse launched September 8, free to start, with a Sentinel system separating what the agent can read from what it can write. OpenAI answered at DevDay with Dots, living inside ChatGPT at $100 a month for Pro, $125 a seat for Business Premium, running on GPT-6 Astra with over 4,000 app connectors. Anthropic just opened the research preview for Claude Duet, built on Opus 5.5, reaching across roughly 6,000 connectors and plugins, included at no extra cost for Pro and Max.

The mechanism is the same everywhere: each agent gets its own cloud computer and browser, keeps working after you close the app, and checks with you before anything consequential happens, like a Stripe payment or a Shop Pay purchase in Duet's case. What differs is distribution. Muse is a standalone app chasing consumers and small business owners. Dots lives where teams already work, in Slack and Teams, with specialist dots and a shared Space on the roadmap. Duet inherits Claude's existing memories and skills, so it's really an upgrade to a relationship people already have rather than a new habit to build.

Reminds me of the smart speaker years, when every major platform shipped a voice assistant within months of each other and the fight wasn't really about who understood language best, it was about who already lived in your house. The agent that already has your calendar, your inbox, your Slack wins by default, not by being smarter.

None of these four has proven it can run unsupervised for a week without creating a mess a human has to clean up. That's the actual product question nobody's answered yet.

https://t.co/3qZO5jXBtk

Read through all 27 incidents and look at the common denominator:

• CAs holding master keys equal to the number 4 (eMudhra) • Hosting providers leaking stored developer secrets (Railway) • Platforms getting wiped out and shutting down (Zeabur) • Autonomous AI agents leaking business secrets (Meta Muse)

The entire internet architecture is built on the fatal assumption that we must surrender our data, keys, and trust to centralized servers and corporate gatekeepers.

When the hosting company goes down or the CA gets cracked, your audit trails and provenance vanish.The antidote is Zero-Custody, Zero-Knowledge architecture: 

1. Files & secrets never leave local silicon (client-side hashing).

2. Proofs are anchored not to a corporate server, but to 800+ exahashes of Bitcoin proof-of-work.

3. Sub-second agent execution (T_index​) fossilized so AI cannot rewrite history.

If Zeabur shuts down tomorrow, your proof survives. If eMudhra leaks another integer, math doesn't break.

Don't trust servers. Verify the blocks.
